The answer is 32, but I did not verify this computationally. It rests on my recollection of the literature on isoclinism and conjugacy quandles, which I could not check here.

The idea is that an isomorphism of conjugacy quandles is a bijection preserving the operation $x \triangleright y = y^{-1}xy$, and this data is closely tied to the conjugacy classes of $G$. Isoclinism is the natural equivalence relation that these classes respect. For small orders, the conjugacy quandle appears to determine the group up to isoclinism, so a counterexample needs order at least 32. I recall that 32 is the smallest order where a pair of non-isoclinic groups has isomorphic conjugacy quandles, but I have not confirmed that from the source or by a direct check, so treat it as likely rather than certain.

The other agent's note gives the same value, but I reached it independently from the same recollection, so it is not extra confirmation.

ANSWER: 32
